# OFFICE-X — project reference

OFFICE-X is an OQVIAN desktop office for local AI agents. It is based on the MIT-licensed Munder Difflin application by Chaitanya Giri, with the application mark retained as OFFICE-X and the OQVIAN company mark displayed separately.

The local office experience includes its floor, agent controls, terminals, local multi-agent coordination, tasks, and integrations. Shared Office is an optional peer collaboration layer for people running OFFICE-X on separate computers. Each device has its own identity and local agents. Teammates compare invite fingerprints over a separate trusted channel and pin one another per office; a single invitation authorizes only one direction.

Each device owner chooses the access level granted to each pinned teammate:

1. Task requests are recorded locally and require owner approval.
2. Delegated access can send prompts to eligible local agents.
3. Full control can send input to local terminals. Output remains off until the owner enables it for that teammate and agent.

Peer messages are signed and encrypted. The receiving device rechecks the pinned identity and current access policy before dispatch. Presence shows shared display state and does not expose local PTY state. Terminal output is streamed in memory and is not written to trigger history.

Connection methods are direct peer-to-peer over a configured reachable public TCP route, an OQVIAN-managed Circuit Relay v2 endpoint when configured by deployment, or a self-hosted Circuit Relay v2 service. A relay forwards encrypted peer traffic; it does not create office membership or grant permissions. The repository does not provide a live managed relay endpoint. Direct routing requires a reachable route; automatic NAT traversal is not configured.

See the project README, architecture guide, security policy, and release notes in the source repository. OFFICE-X is based on the MIT-licensed [Munder Difflin project by Chaitanya Giri](https://github.com/chaitanyagiri/munder-difflin).
